title: Maximum Sum of Edge Values in a Graph
summary: Given an undirected connected graph with n nodes numbered 0 to n-1, where each node is connected to at most two others, and m edges represented by a 2D array, assign each node a unique value from 1 to n such that the score, defined as the sum of the products of values of nodes connected by each edge, is maximized.
statement: Given an undirected connected graph with n nodes numbered 0 to n-1, where each node is connected to at most two others, and m edges represented by a 2D array, assign each node a unique value from 1 to n such that the score, defined as the sum of the products of values of nodes connected by each edge, is maximized. Return the highest possible score.
constraints: The graph is connected, has up to 50,000 nodes, and every node has degree at most two.
Assign every value from 1 through n to exactly one node.
Maximize the sum of endpoint-value products over all edges.
hints: A connected degree-two graph is either a path or a cycle, so only the best linear or circular ordering of 1..n matters.
Place large values next to other large values using the pendulum ordering; a cycle closes the two smallest endpoints.
Detect a cycle by edges==n, construct the corresponding alternating-parity order, and sum neighboring products.
The rearrangement exchange argument forces larger values to receive larger neighboring sums; the pendulum order satisfies those inequalities and is optimal.
editorial: The rearrangement exchange argument forces larger values to receive larger neighboring sums; the pendulum order satisfies those inequalities and is optimal.

tests.explanation: The graph is a cycle; arranging nearby large values carefully gives score 82.
